sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ dyūtajitāḥ pārthāḥ kopitāś ca durātmabhiḥ dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ sahāmātyair nikṛtyā dvijasattama
english: Janamejaya said: Thus were the Pārthas conquered at dice and provoked by the wicked sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with their ministers through treachery, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: śrāvitāḥ paruṣā vācaḥ sṛjadbhir vairam uttamam kim akurvanta kauravyā mama pūrvapitāmahāḥ
english: Made to hear harsh words by those who were sowing the highest enmity, what did my great forebears, the scions of Kuru, do?

sanskrit: kathaṃ caiśvaryavibhraṣṭāḥ sahasā duḥkham eyuṣaḥ vane vijahrire pārthāḥ śakrapratimatejasaḥ
english: How did the Pārthas, whose splendour rivalled Indra's, suddenly fallen from their sovereignty and plunged into sorrow, pass their time in the forest?

sanskrit: ke cainān anvavartanta prāptān vyasanam uttamam kimāhārāḥ kimācārāḥ kva ca vāso mahātmanām
english: Who followed those great-souled ones when they had met with supreme calamity? What was their food, what their conduct, and where did they dwell?

sanskrit: kathaṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi vane teṣāṃ mahātmanām vyatīyur brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha śūrāṇām arighātinām
english: How did twelve years pass in the forest for those great-souled heroes, O best of brāhmaṇas, who slew their enemies?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca rājaputrī sā pravarā sarvayoṣitām pativratā mahābhāgā satataṃ satyavādinī vanavāsam aduḥkhārhā dāruṇaṃ pratyapadyata
english: And how did that princess, foremost of all women, devoted to her husbands, greatly blessed, ever truthful, she who deserved no suffering, come to endure that harsh forest exile?

sanskrit: etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ vistareṇa tapodhana śrotum icchāmi caritaṃ bhūridraviṇatejasām kathyamānaṃ tvayā vipra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Tell me all this in full detail, O wealth of asceticism; I wish to hear the deeds of those of vast wealth and splendour as narrated by you, O brāhmaṇa — my curiosity is very great.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ dyūtajitāḥ pārthāḥ kopitāś ca durātmabhiḥ dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ sahāmātyair niryayur gajasāhvayāt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus conquered at dice and provoked by the wicked sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with their ministers, the Pārthas departed from the city of the elephant.

sanskrit: vardhamānapuradvāreṇābhiniṣkramya te tadā udaṅmukhāḥ śastrabhṛtaḥ prayayuḥ saha kṛṣṇayā
english: Issuing forth through the gate of the city called Vardhamāna, those weapon-bearing heroes set out facing northward, accompanied by Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: indrasenādayaś cainān bhṛtyāḥ paricaturdaśa rathair anuyayuḥ śīghraiḥ striya ādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: And fourteen servants, led by Indrasena, followed them on swift chariots, taking all the women along.

sanskrit: vrajatas tān viditvā tu paurāḥ śokābhipīḍitāḥ garhayanto 'sakṛd bhīṣmaviduradroṇagautamān ūcur vigatasaṃtrāsāḥ samāgamya parasparam
english: The townspeople, learning of their departure and oppressed by grief, repeatedly censuring Bhīṣma, Vidura, Droṇa, and Gautama, gathered together fearlessly and spoke to one another.

sanskrit: nedam asti kulaṃ sarvaṃ na vayaṃ na ca no gṛhāḥ yatra duryodhanaḥ pāpaḥ saubaleyena pālitaḥ karṇaduḥśāsanābhyāṃ ca rājyam etac cikīrṣati
english: "Neither this entire clan nor we ourselves nor our homes have any worth where the sinful Duryodhana, guided by the son of Subala and by Karṇa and Duḥśāsana, seeks to rule this kingdom."

sanskrit: no cet kulaṃ na cācāro na dharmo 'rthaḥ kutaḥ sukham yatra pāpasahāyo 'yaṃ pāpo rājyaṃ bubhūṣate
english: "Where this sinful man with his sinful allies desires to rule, there is no clan, no righteous conduct, no dharma, no wealth — whence then happiness?"

sanskrit: duryodhano gurudveṣī tyaktācārasuhṛjjanaḥ arthalubdho 'bhimānī ca nīcaḥ prakṛtinirghṛṇaḥ
english: "Duryodhana hates his elders, has abandoned proper conduct and friends, is greedy for wealth, arrogant, base, and naturally without pity."

sanskrit: neyam asti mahī kṛtsnā yatra duryodhano nṛpaḥ sādhu gacchāmahe sarve yatra gacchanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "This whole earth has no worth where Duryodhana is king. Let us all go well wherever the Pāṇḍavas go."

sanskrit: sānukrośā mahātmāno vijitendriyaśatravaḥ hrīmantaḥ kīrtimantaś ca dharmācāraparāyaṇāḥ
english: "They are compassionate, great-souled, conquerors of their senses and their enemies, modest, glorious, and devoted to the practice of dharma."

sanskrit: evam uktvānujagmus tān pāṇḍavāṃs te sametya ca ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve tān kuntīmādrinandanān
english: Having spoken thus, they followed after the Pāṇḍavas, and all gathered together, they addressed those sons of Kuntī and Mādrī with folded hands.

sanskrit: kva gamiṣyatha bhadraṃ vas tyaktvāsmān duḥkhabhāginaḥ vayam apy anuyāsyāmo yatra yūyaṃ gamiṣyatha
english: "Where will you go, may all be well with you, leaving us who share your sorrow? We too shall follow wherever you shall go."

sanskrit: adharmeṇa jitāñ śrutvā yuṣmāṃs tyaktaghṛṇaiḥ paraiḥ udvignāḥ sma bhṛśaṃ sarve nāsmān hātum ihārhatha
english: "Having heard that you were defeated through unrighteousness by enemies devoid of mercy, we are all greatly distressed — you ought not to abandon us here."

sanskrit: bhaktānuraktāḥ suhṛdaḥ sadā priyahite ratān kurājādhiṣṭhite rājye na vinaśyema sarvaśaḥ
english: "Devoted and attached friends, ever intent on your welfare and good — we would all be destroyed in a kingdom ruled by an evil king."

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ cābhidhāsyāmo guṇadoṣān nararṣabhāḥ śubhāśubhādhivāsena saṃsargaṃ kurute yathā
english: "And please listen, O bulls among men, as we describe the virtues and faults, how association with the good or evil shapes one's character."

sanskrit: vastram āpas tilān bhūmiṃ gandho vāsayate yathā puṣpāṇām adhivāsena tathā saṃsargajā guṇāḥ
english: "As fragrance perfumes cloth, water, sesame, and earth through the presence of flowers, so are qualities born of association."

sanskrit: mohajālasya yonir hi mūḍhair eva samāgamaḥ ahany ahani dharmasya yoniḥ sādhusamāgamaḥ
english: "Association with fools is the source of the net of delusion; association with the good is the source of dharma day after day."

sanskrit: tasmāt prājñaiś ca vṛddhaiś ca susvabhāvais tapasvibhiḥ sadbhiś ca saha saṃsargaḥ kāryaḥ śamaparāyaṇaiḥ
english: "Therefore one should seek the company of the wise, the aged, the virtuous, ascetics, the good, and those devoted to tranquillity."

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ trīṇy avadātāni yonir vidyā ca karma ca tān sevet taiḥ samāsyā hi śāstrebhyo 'pi garīyasī
english: "One should associate with those whose three things are pure — birth, knowledge, and conduct — for sitting with them is indeed more valuable than the scriptures themselves."

sanskrit: nirārambhā hy api vayaṃ puṇyaśīleṣu sādhuṣu puṇyam evāpnuyāmeha pāpaṃ pāpopasevanāt
english: "Even without any effort of our own, by associating with those of virtuous nature, the good, we would gain merit here; and sin from attending upon the sinful."

sanskrit: asatāṃ darśanāt sparśāt saṃjalpanasahāsanāt dharmācārāḥ prahīyante na ca sidhyanti mānavāḥ
english: "From the sight, touch, conversation, and laughter shared with the wicked, men's righteous conduct declines and they do not prosper."

sanskrit: buddhiś ca hīyate puṃsāṃ nīcaiḥ saha samāgamāt madhyamair madhyatāṃ yāti śreṣṭhatāṃ yāti cottamaiḥ
english: "A man's intellect degrades by association with the lowly; it reaches a middling state with those of middling quality, and rises to excellence with the excellent."

sanskrit: ye guṇāḥ kīrtitā loke dharmakāmārthasaṃbhavāḥ lokācārātmasaṃbhūtā vedoktāḥ śiṣṭasaṃmatāḥ
english: "The qualities celebrated in the world, arising from dharma, desire, and wealth, born of worldly conduct and self, enjoined by the Vedas and approved by the learned —"

sanskrit: te yuṣmāsu samastāś ca vyastāś caiveha sadguṇāḥ icchāmo guṇavan madhye vastuṃ śreyo 'bhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: "— all those good qualities, both together and separately, are present in you. Desirous of the highest good, we wish to dwell among the virtuous."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhanyā vayaṃ yad asmākaṃ snehakāruṇyayantritāḥ asato 'pi guṇān āhur brāhmaṇapramukhāḥ prajāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: We are blessed that the people, led by the brāhmaṇas, moved by love and compassion, speak of virtues even in us who have none.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ bhrātṛsahitaḥ sarvān vijñāpayāmi vaḥ nānyathā tad dhi kartavyam asmatsnehānukampayā
english: Therefore I, together with my brothers, make this request to you all: it must not be done otherwise — out of love and compassion for us.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ pitāmaho rājā viduro jananī ca me suhṛjjanaś ca prāyo me nagare nāgasāhvaye
english: My grandfather Bhīṣma, the king, Vidura, my mother, and the greater part of my dear ones remain in the city of Hastināpura.

sanskrit: te tv asmaddhitakāmārthaṃ pālanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ yuṣmābhiḥ sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ śokasaṃtāpavihvalāḥ
english: They, overwhelmed with grief and anguish, are to be carefully attended to and protected by all of you together for the sake of our welfare.

sanskrit: nivartatāgatā dūraṃ samāgamanaśāpitāḥ svajane nyāsabhūte me kāryā snehānvitā matiḥ
english: Turn back — you have come far enough, I adjure you by our reunion; my mind, filled with love, must be fixed upon my own people who are left as a trust.

sanskrit: etad dhi mama kāryāṇāṃ paramaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam sukṛtānena me tuṣṭiḥ satkāraś ca bhaviṣyati
english: This, indeed, is what lies highest in my heart among all my duties; by this good act both my satisfaction and honour will come about.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathānumantritās tena dharmarājena tāḥ prajāḥ cakrur ārtasvaraṃ ghoraṃ hā rājann iti duḥkhitāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus dismissed by the king of dharma, those people, grieving, raised a terrible cry of anguish: "Alas, O king!"

sanskrit: guṇān pārthasya saṃsmṛtya duḥkhārtāḥ paramāturāḥ akāmāḥ saṃnyavartanta samāgamyātha pāṇḍavān
english: Remembering the virtues of the son of Pṛthā, wracked with sorrow and utterly distressed, they unwillingly turned back after approaching the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: nivṛtteṣu tu paureṣu rathān āsthāya pāṇḍavāḥ prajagmur jāhnavītīre pramāṇākhyaṃ mahāvaṭam
english: When the townspeople had turned back, the Pāṇḍavas mounted their chariots and proceeded to the great banyan tree on the bank of the Jāhnavī called Pramāṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ te divasaśeṣeṇa vaṭaṃ gatvā tu pāṇḍavāḥ ūṣus tāṃ rajanīṃ vīrāḥ saṃspṛśya salilaṃ śuci udakenaiva tāṃ rātrim ūṣus te duḥkhakarśitāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas reached that banyan tree with the remainder of the day; those heroes touched the pure water and spent that night there — afflicted by sorrow, they passed that night sustained by water alone.

sanskrit: anujagmuś ca tatraitān snehāt ke cid dvijātayaḥ sāgnayo 'nagnayaś caiva saśiṣyagaṇabāndhavāḥ sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā śuśubhe brahmavādibhiḥ
english: Certain twice-born ones followed them there out of love — some with their sacred fires, some without, along with their circles of pupils and kinsmen; the king, surrounded by those speakers of Brahman, shone forth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prāduṣkṛtāgnīnāṃ muhūrte ramyadāruṇe brahmaghoṣapuraskāraḥ saṃjalpaḥ samajāyata
english: When their fires were kindled at an hour both delightful and awesome, conversation arose, led by the sound of Vedic recitation.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ tu kuruśreṣṭhaṃ te haṃsamadhurasvarāḥ āśvāsayanto viprāgryāḥ kṣapāṃ sarvāṃ vyanodayan
english: Those eminent brāhmaṇas, with voices sweet as swans, consoling the foremost king of the Kurus, passed the entire night.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām vanaṃ yiyāsatāṃ viprās tasthur bhikṣābhujo 'grataḥ tān uvāca tato rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When dawn came, brāhmaṇas who lived on alms stood in front of those whose deeds are untiring, as they were about to set out for the forest. Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, addressed them.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi hṛtasarvasvā hṛtarājyā hṛtaśriyaḥ phalamūlāmiṣāhārā vanaṃ yāsyāma duḥkhitāḥ
english: "We are utterly stripped of everything — our kingdom taken, our fortune taken; we shall go to the forest in sorrow, to live on fruits, roots, and meat."

sanskrit: vanaṃ ca doṣabahulaṃ bahuvyālasarīsṛpam parikleśaś ca vo manye dhruvaṃ tatra bhaviṣyati
english: "The forest is full of dangers, with many serpents and crawling creatures, and I believe hardship there for you will certainly come to pass."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ parikleśo daivatāny api sādayet kiṃ punar mām ito viprā nivartadhvaṃ yatheṣṭataḥ
english: "The affliction of brāhmaṇas would distress even the gods — how much more so me. Therefore, O brāhmaṇas, return from here as you please."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ gatir yā bhavatāṃ rājaṃs tāṃ vayaṃ gantum udyatāḥ nārhathāsmān parityaktuṃ bhaktān saddharmadarśinaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas said: Whatever path is yours, O king, we are ready to take it; you ought not to abandon us who are devoted to you and see the true dharma.

sanskrit: anukampāṃ hi bhakteṣu daivatāny api kurvate viśeṣato brāhmaṇeṣu sadācārāvalambiṣu
english: "Even the gods show compassion to the devoted — especially to brāhmaṇas who hold to right conduct."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mamāpi paramā bhaktir brāhmaṇeṣu sadā dvijāḥ sahāyaviparibhraṃśas tv ayaṃ sādayatīva mām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: My devotion to brāhmaṇas too is always supreme, O twice-born ones; but this loss of resources to provide for attendants grieves me deeply.

sanskrit: āhareyur hi me ye 'pi phalamūlamṛgāṃs tathā ta ime śokajair duḥkhair bhrātaro me vimohitāḥ
english: "Those brothers of mine who might have gathered fruits, roots, and game for me — even they are bewildered by sorrows born of grief."

sanskrit: draupadyā viprakarṣeṇa rājyāpaharaṇena ca duḥkhānvitān imān kleśair nāhaṃ yoktum ihotsahe
english: "I cannot bring myself to add hardships to these men already afflicted with sorrow — because of the outrage done to Draupadī and the theft of the kingdom."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ asmatpoṣaṇajā cintā mā bhūt te hṛdi pārthiva svayam āhṛtya vanyāni anuyāsyāmahe vayam
english: The brāhmaṇas said: Let no anxiety about our sustenance lodge in your heart, O king; we ourselves shall bring forest provisions and follow along with you.

sanskrit: anudhyānena japyena vidhāsyāmaḥ śivaṃ tava kathābhiś cānukūlābhiḥ saha raṃsyāmahe vane
english: "Through meditation and chanting we shall bring about your well-being, and with agreeable stories we shall take delight together in the forest."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam etan na saṃdeho rameyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha nyūnabhāvāt tu paśyāmi pratyādeśam ivātmanaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: There is no doubt that I would rejoice in the company of brāhmaṇas; yet because of my deficiency I see it as a kind of reproach to myself.

sanskrit: kathaṃ drakṣyāmi vaḥ sarvān svayam āhṛtabhojanān madbhaktyā kliśyato 'narhān dhik pāpān dhṛtarāṣṭrajān
english: "How shall I look upon you all fetching your own food, suffering hardship in devotion to me, you who deserve no such hardship? Shame on the sinful sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā sa nṛpaḥ śocan niṣasāda mahītale tam adhyātmaratir vidvāñ śaunako nāma vai dvijaḥ yoge sāṃkhye ca kuśalo rājānam idam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the king, sorrowing, sat down upon the earth. Then a learned twice-born named Śaunaka, delighting in the knowledge of the self and skilled in Yoga and Sāṃkhya, spoke thus to the king.

sanskrit: śokasthānasahasrāṇi bhayasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: Thousands of grounds for grief and hundreds of grounds for fear enter the fool day after day — not the wise man.

sanskrit: na hi jñānaviruddheṣu bahudoṣeṣu karmasu śreyoghātiṣu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ
english: For the intelligent, men of your kind, do not cling to actions that are contrary to wisdom, fraught with many faults, and destructive of the highest good.

sanskrit: aṣṭāṅgāṃ buddhim āhur yāṃ sarvāśreyovighātinīm śrutismṛtisamāyuktāṃ sā rājaṃs tvayy avasthitā
english: That eightfold intellect which is joined with what has been heard and remembered, and which they say destroys all that is inauspicious — that, O king, is established in you.

sanskrit: arthakṛcchreṣu durgeṣu vyāpatsu svajanasya ca śārīramānasair duḥkhair na sīdanti bhavadvidhāḥ
english: Men of your kind do not sink under difficulties of wealth, calamities, afflictions of kinsmen, or sufferings of body and mind.

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ cābhidhāsyāmi janakena yathā purā ātmavyavasthānakarā gītāḥ ślokā mahātmanā
english: And please listen as I recite the verses that the great-souled Janaka formerly sang, establishing the self in its proper station.

sanskrit: manodehasamutthābhyāṃ duḥkhābhyām arditaṃ jagat tayor vyāsasamāsābhyāṃ śamopāyam imaṃ śṛṇu
english: The world is tormented by two kinds of suffering — that arising from mind and that from body; hear this means of tranquillity concerning them both, in detail and in brief.

sanskrit: vyādher aniṣṭasaṃsparśāc chramād iṣṭavivarjanāt duḥkhaṃ caturbhiḥ śārīraṃ kāraṇaiḥ saṃpravartate
english: Bodily suffering arises from four causes: disease, contact with the unpleasant, fatigue, and separation from what is dear.

sanskrit: tad āśupratikārāc ca satataṃ cāvicintanāt ādhivyādhipraśamanaṃ kriyāyogadvayena tu
english: The calming of mental and bodily afflictions comes through two forms of action: swift remedying of the cause, and constant non-dwelling upon it in thought.

sanskrit: matimanto hy ato vaidyāḥ śamaṃ prāg eva kurvate mānasasya priyākhyānaiḥ saṃbhogopanayair nṛṇām
english: Therefore intelligent physicians first bring about relief of the mental suffering of men by means of pleasing narrations and the introduction of enjoyments.

sanskrit: mānasena hi duḥkhena śarīram upatapyate ayaḥpiṇḍena taptena kumbhasaṃstham ivodakam
english: For the body is tormented by mental suffering just as water in a pot is heated by a ball of hot iron.

sanskrit: mānasaṃ śamayet tasmāj jñānenāgnim ivāmbunā praśānte mānase duḥkhe śārīram upaśāmyati
english: Therefore one should calm the mental suffering with knowledge, as one quenches fire with water; when the mental suffering is pacified, the bodily suffering subsides.

sanskrit: manaso duḥkhamūlaṃ tu sneha ity upalabhyate snehāt tu sajjate jantur duḥkhayogam upaiti ca
english: The root of mental suffering is understood to be attachment; through attachment a being becomes ensnared and comes to encounter suffering.

sanskrit: snehamūlāni duḥkhāni snehajāni bhayāni ca śokaharṣau tathāyāsaḥ sarvaṃ snehāt pravartate
english: Sorrows are rooted in attachment; fears too are born of attachment; grief and joy alike, and weariness — everything proceeds from attachment.

sanskrit: snehāt karaṇarāgaś ca prajajñe vaiṣayas tathā aśreyaskāv ubhāv etau pūrvas tatra guruḥ smṛtaḥ
english: From attachment also arose passion of the senses and sensuality; both of these lead away from the good, and the former is considered the greater of the two.

sanskrit: koṭarāgnir yathāśeṣaṃ samūlaṃ pādapaṃ dahet dharmārthinaṃ tathālpo 'pi rāgadoṣo vināśayet
english: As a fire in the hollow of a tree burns the entire tree down to its roots, so even a small fault of passion destroys one who aspires to dharma.

sanskrit: viprayoge na tu tyāgī doṣadarśī samāgamāt virāgaṃ bhajate jantur nirvairo niṣparigrahaḥ
english: A being who sees the fault in union but does not renounce at separation comes to dispassion — free of enmity, free of possessions.

sanskrit: tasmāt snehaṃ svapakṣebhyo mitrebhyo dhanasaṃcayāt svaśarīrasamutthaṃ tu jñānena vinivartayet
english: Therefore one should, by means of knowledge, withdraw attachment from one's own side, from friends, from accumulation of wealth, and that which arises from one's own body.

sanskrit: jñānānviteṣu mukhyeṣu śāstrajñeṣu kṛtātmasu na teṣu sajjate snehaḥ padmapatreṣv ivodakam
english: In those foremost ones endowed with knowledge, learned in the scriptures, and of purified self, attachment does not cling — like water on a lotus leaf.

sanskrit: rāgābhibhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ kāmena parikṛṣyate icchā saṃjāyate tasya tatas tṛṣṇā pravartate
english: A man overwhelmed by passion is dragged along by desire; from that desire arises craving, and from that craving thirst spreads further.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇā hi sarvapāpiṣṭhā nityodvegakarī nṛṇām adharmabahulā caiva ghorā pāpānubandhinī
english: Thirst indeed is the most sinful of all things, ever causing agitation in men, abounding in unrighteousness, terrible, and bound up with sin.

sanskrit: yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ yo 'sau prāṇāntiko rogas tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham
english: That which is hard to abandon for the foolish-minded, which does not decay even as the body decays, which is that life-ending disease — happiness comes to one who abandons that thirst.

sanskrit: anādyantā tu sā tṛṣṇā antardehagatā nṛṇām vināśayati saṃbhūtā ayonija ivānalaḥ
english: That thirst, without beginning or end, lodged within the body of men, once arisen, destroys them — like fire born without a womb.

sanskrit: yathaidhaḥ svasamutthena vahninā nāśam ṛcchati tathākṛtātmā lobhena sahajena vinaśyati
english: As firewood meets destruction by the fire that arises from itself, so the undisciplined self is destroyed by its innate greed.
